questions.q: What is the "Climate Change Act of 2009"?
questions.n: This is the specific Republic Act number assigned to the Climate Change Act of 2009.

questions.q: Is the Green Building Code intended to rate buildings?
o: Yes, but only for buildings exceeding 20,000 sqm.
No, because it only applies to government-owned structures.
Yes, it provides a scoring system similar to LEED and BERDE.
No, because it is a set of regulations setting minimum standards for compliance.
questions.n: The Green Building Code establishes mandatory minimums rather than competitive ratings.

questions.q: Minimum TGFA for malls to apply Building Code:
questions.n: This is the specific Total Gross Floor Area threshold for the 'Mall' category under the code.

questions.q: Minimum TGFA for Hospitals to apply Building Code:
questions.n: Hospitals must comply with the code if they meet or exceed this TGFA.

questions.q: Minimum TGFA for Condominiums to apply Building Code:
questions.n: Condominiums fall under the 20,000 sqm threshold for compliance.

questions.q: What does BRI stand for?
questions.n: This is the technical/medical term used to describe health issues caused by building environments.

questions.q: Parts of the building used by the occupants, owners, tenants or other building users of which the landlord retains control and is responsible to maintain in a reasonably safe condition that includes spaces such as lobby, corridor, hallway, toilet, elevator or stairway:
questions.n: Common areas are the shared spaces maintained by the landlord for all building users.

questions.q: Mixture of various organic substances that can be placed into a composition of decaying biodegradable materials which eventually turns into a nutrient-rich material, used for fertilizing soil:
questions.n: This term specifically refers to organic materials that decompose into nutrient-rich compost.

questions.q: An area substantially illuminated by daylight consistently receiving significant quantities of daylight during the day:
questions.n: The daylight zone is the interior area that relies on natural light from windows or skylights.

questions.q: Energy efficiency rating for room air conditioners that lists how many Btu per hour are used for each watt of power it draws:
questions.n: EER is the standard ratio used to measure the cooling efficiency of air conditioners.

questions.q: A horizontal surface that reflects daylight deep into a building, placed above eye-level with high-reflectance upper surfaces, which reflect daylight onto the ceiling and deeper into the space:
questions.n: A light shelf is a horizontal device used to bounce natural light deeper into a room.

questions.q: Amount of electric lighting, usually measured in watts per square foot, being used to illuminate a given space:
questions.n: LPD measures the electrical load of lighting per unit of area.

questions.q: A facility designed to receive, sort, process, and store compostable and recyclable materials efficiently and in an environmentally sound manner:
questions.n: MRFs are the designated centers for processing recyclable and compostable waste.

questions.q: Resistance value or the capacity to resist heat loss or its thermal resistance:
questions.n: R-value specifically denotes the thermal resistance of a material.

questions.q: An industrial structure designed to remove biological or chemical waste products from water, thereby permitting the treated water to be used for other purposes:
questions.n: An STP processes wastewater to remove contaminants for safe reuse or disposal.

questions.q: A measure of a material’s ability to reflect heat with white or light colors having high reflectance and dark or black surfaces with low or little reflectance thereby having higher temperatures:
questions.n: Solar Reflectance Index (SRI) combines reflectivity and emissivity to measure heat rejection.

questions.q: Combination of urea and formaldehyde used in some glues and adhesives, particularly in composite wood products, emitting formaldehyde at room temperature, which is a toxic and possibly carcinogenic gas:
questions.n: This specific adhesive is a major source of indoor air pollution and off-gassing.

questions.q: Employs frequency inverter technology which regulates input voltage and frequency throughout the journey, drawing much less current during acceleration and deceleration:
questions.n: VVVF drives provide smooth control and high energy efficiency for motors and elevators.

questions.q: The ratio of total transmitted light to total incident light with the higher value allowing more incident light to pass through the glazing:
questions.n: Visible Transmittance (VT) measures the amount of light that enters through a window.

questions.q: Organic chemicals which have a high vapor pressure at ordinary room temperature that are dangerous to human health or cause harm to the environment:
questions.n: VOCs are chemicals that evaporate easily and can impact indoor air quality.

questions.q: Ratio of the total area of a building facade, which is occupied by windows (glass area and frame):
questions.n: Window-to-Wall Ratio (WWR) is the percentage of the facade that is transparent.

questions.q: Which material transmits more heat?
questions.n: Glass typically has higher thermal transmittance (U-value) and allows solar radiation to pass through.

questions.q: Heat transmitted through glass divided by radiation incident on glass:
questions.n: Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (SHGC) represents the fraction of solar radiation admitted through a window.

questions.q: Composting by Earthworms is called as:
questions.n: Vermicomposting specifically refers to the use of worms to break down organic matter.

questions.q: LCA stands for:
questions.n: LCA is the process of evaluating the environmental impact of a product throughout its entire life.

questions.q: Minimum air space for Workshops, Factories, and Offices is ___ cubic meters of air space per person:
questions.n: The standard requirement is 12.00 cubic meters of air space per person for these occupancies.

questions.q: Maximum Allowable PSO (percentage site occupancy) for Institutional with firewall:
questions.n: The maximum PSO for institutional developments with a firewall is 70%.

questions.q: Attempts to safeguard air, water, and earth by choosing eco-friendly building materials and construction practices:
questions.n: Green Architecture focuses on reducing environmental impact through design and materials.

questions.q: Door Leaf Width. No leaf of an exit door shall exceed ___ meters in width:
questions.n: According to the code, a single leaf of an exit door cannot exceed 1.20 meters.

questions.q: The term usually applies to the surfaces of terrestrial and glaciated environments, but it could also pertain to the surfaces of oceans and other bodies of water:
questions.n: This is the term associated with this description in the provided context.

questions.q: A building material which is one of the poorest conductors of heat:
questions.n: Wood has natural insulating properties and is a poor conductor compared to metal or stone.

questions.q: An independent art gallery run by the various artist to provide spaces to showcase Arts:
questions.n: Artist-run spaces are galleries managed directly by the creators.

questions.q: A technique that efficiently brings light into your home using exterior glazing (windows, skylights, etc.), thereby reducing artificial lighting requirements and saving energy:
questions.n: Day lighting is the practice of placing windows and reflective surfaces to use natural light.

questions.q: The process of supplying air to and removing air from an indoor space without using mechanical systems:
questions.n: Natural ventilation uses pressure differences to move air without mechanical help.

questions.q: Integrates architecture and sculpture and is often embellished with rosettes, scrolls, pediments and Solomonic columns which may be gilded or polychromed:
questions.n: A retablo is the ornate structure behind an altar, characteristic of Spanish Baroque influence.

questions.q: The ability of a material to absorb and store heat energy:
questions.n: Thermal mass refers to a material's capacity to store heat and release it slowly.

questions.q: BERDE has an Innovation category, and LEED does not:
questions.n: Both BERDE and LEED have categories that reward innovative green building practices.

questions.q: What specific type of architecture did the Spanish colonizers apply to the designs and structures in the country?
questions.n: Antillian refers to the Caribbean-influenced Spanish colonial style seen in the Philippines.

questions.q: MORE WALLS ON HOUSES NOT ONLY ALLOW AIR TO CIRCULATE FREELY, IT ALSO MAKES THE ROOM LOOK BIG AND SPACIOUS:
questions.n: Fewer walls and open plans are what allow for free air circulation and a spacious feel.

questions.q: In reference to tropical design and stilt houses, which climate is being discussed?
questions.n: Tropical climates use stilts for ventilation and to avoid dampness and flooding.

questions.q: Any climatic condition in a relatively small area, within a few metres or less above and below the Earth’s surface and within canopies of vegetation:
questions.n: Microclimate describes the specific weather conditions of a very localized area.

questions.q: The ability to be maintained at a certain rate or level; meeting our present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs:
questions.n: Sustainability is defined by balancing current needs with the needs of the future.

questions.q: Which statement accurately describes LEED?
o: A mandatory Philippine building code for all residential homes.
A government regulation focusing solely on water conservation in the UK.
A local rating system developed by the Philippine Green Building Council.
Program—An independent certification program developed by the U.S. Green Building Council.
questions.n: This correctly identifies LEED as an independent, USGBC-developed rating system.

questions.q: The design of products and environments to be usable by all people, to the greatest extent possible, without the need for adaptation or specialized design:
questions.n: Universal Design aims to make environments accessible to all users regardless of ability.

questions.q: Air Conditioning accounts for more than ____% of total electricity costs in a centrally air conditioned building:
questions.n: AC typically accounts for over half of the energy consumption in centralized systems.

questions.q: One of the most important aspects of the design of a Green Building is the implementation of low impact, renewable and sustainable energy sources. Which of the following is not an ideal energy source for a Green Building?
questions.n: Natural gas is a non-renewable fossil fuel and is not considered an 'ideal' sustainable source.

questions.q: Distance of Outdoor Smoking Area from building Opening:
questions.n: The standard requirement is a 10-meter clearance from any building opening.

questions.q: Promote energy efficiency by reducing unnecessary power consumption for lighting, contributing to more sustainable and cost effective building operation:
questions.n: LPD is the metric used to ensure lighting systems are designed efficiently.

questions.q: Overhead/elevated water storage shall be integrated in the water distribution system. Buildings below how many storeys are exempted?
questions.n: Buildings with fewer than 10 storeys (per code) or 4 storeys (per context provided) are often exempted.

questions.q: Escalators / Moving Ramps / Walkways shall be fitted with automated controls to reduce to a slower speed when no activity has been detected for a maximum period of:
questions.n: Controls must slow down the equipment after 1.5 minutes of inactivity to save energy.
